request.description:
`open`'s request: open a document's file as a session, or make a new, empty one, at a
path or, with `path` null, untitled. A document the gate refuses still opens, its
problems in the result, so it can be mended with `replace_text`.

create.description:
Whether to make a new, empty document at the path: refused if anything is there.
Must be true when `path` is null.

path.description:
The document's path, as every response names the session's: a regular file, if it
isn't to be made. A file this process holds open in another session, by any name, is
refused. Null, with `create` true, for an untitled document: an empty one with no
file, nothing written until a `commit` gives it a path (Save As). Outside a
transaction an edit is saved as it's made, so an untitled document's edits are made
inside one.

request.title: OpenRequest

Error.description:
Why a command was refused, or a problem it found, in Silico's error contract: a code, a
message, and, where they apply, the feature, the elements at fault (the first of them, and
how many in all), the request's field at fault, the cause, what to do, and the names that
might have been meant. Every field is always present: null, or empty, where it doesn't
apply.

advice.description:
What the suggestion advises, as data, for a kernel fault whose worker said:
`change_the_values` (the request's values crashed the worker, and would again: change
them, never retry as is), `simplify_or_wait` (it ran past its time: simplify the
operation, or try again), `try_again` (it wasn't the values: try the request again),
or `try_once_more` (only once more: the worker may have been stopped for the memory
the request used). Null for any other error, and a fault whose advice is in its
suggestion's words alone.

candidates.description: What might have been meant, such as the names nearest one that found nothing.

cause.description: What lay under it, such as the kernel's own failure, if known.

code.description: What kind of error it is: one of Silico's error codes, such as `invalid_input`.

elements.description: The elements at fault, by name: the first of them, if there are many.

elements_total.description: How many elements are at fault, listed or not.

feature.description: The ID of the feature at fault, if one is.

message.description: What went wrong, in a sentence.

parameter.description: The field at fault, as a dotted path (`position.2`), if one is.

ranking.description:
Why each candidate is where it is, one a candidate, in their order: what it's made
from that the broken name is (`shared`), what of the broken name it isn't
(`unshared`), whether it's the name's own feature's, and, for a name by number that
finds nothing, the nearest number and its gap. Empty where the candidates follow
another rule, which the suggestion states.

suggestion.description: What to do about it, if Silico can say.

FeatureId.description: A feature's ID: 8 characters of Crockford's base32 in lower case (digits and letters but i, l, o, and u).

Nearest.description: A candidate's element numbered nearest a broken name by number.

element.description: The element, by its own name (`k7f2qx3m.box.Face6`).

gap.description: How many numbers apart it and the broken name are.

Rank.description:
Why a candidate for a broken name is where it is among them. The candidates' order
follows from it: more `shared` first, then `same_feature`, then by name.

nearest.description:
For a name by number that finds nothing and shares nothing with any element, the
candidate's element numbered nearest it, and how far; null otherwise.

same_feature.description: Whether the candidate is an element of the broken name's own feature.

shared.description:
The elements both the candidate's name and the broken one are made from, by their
own names (a sketch's element by its ID), whole, in the names' order.

unshared.description:
The broken name's other elements, in the names' order: with `shared`, every element
the broken name is made from.

result.description: `open`'s result. The response's `session` is the session opened.

bodies.description:
The bodies the timeline ends with: the solids no later feature consumed, in timeline
order, found without a kernel.

features.description: How many features the document has: null if its text doesn't read as a document.

path.description: The path, as given: null for an untitled document.

problems.description:
The gate's problems with the document, the first 100. A document with any still
opens, and the commands that need a document the gate took refuse until
`replace_text` mends it.

problems_total.description: How many problems there are, listed or not.

result.title: OpenResult
